title: Kinetic Region Handoff: SLO-driven capacity-aware steering and soft-circuit playbook
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: We currently have independent region routers that prefer low latency but lack a graded handoff mechanism when capacity or latency degrades. This causes either abrupt client errors (hard failover) or suboptimal ejection decisions that bounce traffic aggressively and increase tail latency. Goal: Build a kinetic region handoff controller that uses SLO signals, short-term capacity probes, and per-customer geo-anchors to perform gradual, reversible traffic migration with integrated soft-circuit breakers and bounded load shedding. The controller should maintain application SLOs (p50/p95/p99 latency targets and error budget burn constraints) while minimizing cross-region hops, honoring customer geo-pinning preferences, and providing an observable, debuggable failover path.
acceptance_criteria: 1) P95 tail latency for routed requests meets configured SLO within 2% under normal traffic after rollout (measured over 24h),
2) Regional failover transitions complete with graceful degradation (at most 10% additional token shedding per minute during migration) and no hard 5xx spikes >1% above baseline,
3) Controller respects explicit customer geo-anchors: customers with pin=strong should not be relocated without manual override, pin=soft allows progressive migration,
4) Circuit breaker triggers are bounded and reversible: when a region crosses capacity score threshold, traffic reduces using proportional soft-drain (not abrupt cut) within 30s,
5) Canaries and synthetic probes detect misrouting in <5m and automated rollback runs within 10m when anomalies exceed tolerance,
6) New metrics available in Console: region_affinity_score, region_capacity_score, handoff_progress_pct, soft_shed_rate, slo_burn_rate, and routing_decision_trace_id for every routed request.
design_summary: Architecture: A decentralized controller per-edge that subscribes to global region capacity broadcasts and local SLO monitors. Each controller computes a weighted score per region: score = latency_penalty * w_lat + capacity_headroom * w_cap + geo_affinity * w_geo + cost_hint * w_cost.

Soft-circuit: Instead of hard ejection, implement a tokenized soft-circuit that reduces admission to a region by decrementing an adjustable token quota (leaky-bucket) and applying traffic diversion ratios progressively (10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100%),

Capacity probing: Periodic lightweight capacity probes (small synthetic requests) to estimate per-region effective concurrency and tail-latency slope; combine with telemetry from serving runtime (active GPU load, queue length, kv-cache hit ratio) to produce region_capacity_score,

Geo-anchors: Per-customer policy (strong/soft/none). Strong => sticky session headers + route affinity enforced unless explicit manual evacuation. Soft => controller will shift with escalation policy but will bias initial routing to origin region,

SLO integration: Evaluate routing decisions against short-term SLO burn (5m, 1h windows). If burn exceeds threshold, prefer safer regions and enable increased token shedding rather than moving more traffic into stressed regions,
Observability: Propagate routing_decision_trace_id in logs/headers; add dashboards and latency burn heatmaps; record decision rationale (scores) for each change for post-mortem.
rollout_plan: Phase 0: Feature flag gated rollout to internal infra and one low-traffic customer org. Verify metrics and decision traces for 48h.
Phase 1: Canary on 5% platform traffic across three non-production regions. Run chaos tests (region CPU throttling, queue saturation) and confirm graceful handoff behavior.
Phase 2: Gradual increase to 25% with live customers (opt-in), enable soft-circuit defaults, and tune weights based on observed handoff_progress_pct and slo_burn_rate.
Phase 3: Full rollout default behavior, expose per-customer pinning controls in Console with audit log entries for manual overrides.

Rollback policy: Immediate disable of kinetic handoff flag reverts to previous weighted-latency router; automated rollback trigger when synthetic canary failures exceed 0.5% or SLO burn sustained >5% over 30m.
testing_plan: Load tests: Gradually increase qps while intentionally starving target region with synthetic load to validate soft-drain ratios and shedding limits.
Chaos scenarios: network partition between regions, region-wide increased p99 due to KV cache miss storm, and delayed capacity broadcasts. Verify recovery and bounded client impact.
SLO smoke tests: Inject latency spikes and confirm routing shifts preserve p95 target for critical tenants designated in testbed.
Integration: End-to-end tests with Console dashboards, logging, and tracing; ensure routing_decision_trace_id maps to a single decision document for each request in observability storage.
monitoring_and_alerting: New metrics: region_capacity_score, region_affinity_score, handoff_progress_pct, soft_shed_rate, routing_decision_rate, routing_rollback_count.
Alerts: region_capacity_score < 0.2 for >2m => paging; slo_burn_rate > threshold for 15m => page on-call and mark handoff as in-progress; automated_rollback_count > 3 in 1h => escalate to SRE.
Dashboards: per-region time-series with decision heatmaps, per-customer pin adherence panel, and canary health summary.
open_questions: Q1: How do we weight cost_hint vs latency when a cheaper region has slightly higher p95 but much lower cost? (proposed: make cost_hint influence only when SLO headroom > 2x),
Q2: Should soft-drain token quotas be per-route or global per-region? Initial plan: per-route with fallback global cap for safety.
Q3: What is the appropriate probe frequency to avoid probe-induced load on small regions? (proposed: adaptive backoff based on recent probe variance),
Q4: Compliance: for customers on Private deployments, how is geo-anchoring enforced across VPC-to-VPC tunnels? Need security review if region affinity header can cross boundaries.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Decision oscillation (flip-flop) between regions under borderline conditions. Mitigation: hysteresis windows, minimum dwell time, and gradual step sizes for soft-drain ratios.
Risk: Synthetic probes add noise and distort capacity view. Mitigation: adaptive probe rate and probe isolation namespace so probes do not evict real requests from cache-sensitive regions.
Risk: Misrouted traffic violates compliance geo constraints. Mitigation: honor strong pins absolutely; add audit trail and automated reversion for flagged violations.
